statement: LEGA-C, 140 passive galaxies. "The galaxies are divided into two stellar velocity dispersion subsamples using their median <sigma_star> = 215 km s-1. For each sigma_star regime, we evaluate the median age in four narrow redshift bins"; constant bin width dz ~ 0.075 (~0.4 Gyr of cosmic time); bin error is the median standard error from the NMAD. The two age-z relations are "approximately parallel and with an offset of Delta age ~ 0.5 Gyr ... consistent with the mass-downsizing scenario".

"Delta z/Delta age is measured from the median age-redshift relation between the ith and the i + 2th points for each sigma_star subsample, and is defined at an effective redshift of z_eff = (z_i + z_{i+2})/2", alternate points so that the age evolution is larger than the statistical scatter; four H(z) estimates (Table 1); low and high sigma_star agree, "their mean values being within 0.1 sigma"; variance-weighted average gives H(z = 0.75) = 98.8 +- 24.8 (stat) km/s/Mpc.

Systematic 22.7 km/s/Mpc: "about 1/3 for the Lick index combination, 1/4 for the binning and for the SPS model, and 1/6 for the SFH"; total H(z = 0.75) = 98.8 +- 33.6. Linear fits to the unbinned age-z relations are used for the index-set test only. H_lo(0.75) = 101.4 +- 34.0, H_hi(0.75) = 96.1 +- 36.3; "H_hi is 5% lower than H_lo and only 3% lower than the final H(z)"; cuts at the 40th and 30th percentile in sigma_star are "consistent within 0.2 sigma".

"a residual evolution in terms of new stars being formed over cosmic time would result in a flatter age-redshift relation and in a higher H(z)". Handled by sample purity (NUVrJ, [O II]/[O III] emission-line cut, visual inspection; 1622 -> 140 galaxies) and by the comparison of the two sigma_star regimes.

Purity cuts: NUVrJ of Ilbert+2013, (NUV - r) > 3 (r - J) + 1 and (NUV - r) > 3.1 (658 sources); EW[O II] > 5 A excluded (485); visual inspection removes strong [O II] 3727 and/or [O III] 5007 (350 passive galaxies). "a cut in H/K < 1.1 can be used jointly with other criteria".

LEGA-C, 335 galaxies at 0.6 <= z <= 1.0, sigma_star threshold 208 km/s. Median age per bin, error "sigma = MAD/sqrt(N)", no weighted average because ages and their errors correlate. Tested N_zbin in {4, 2, 1} x N_sigma-bin in {2, 1}, quantile and fixed bins; "approximately an average of 40 galaxies per bin in the case of 4x2 bins".

"we do not use consecutive bins ... estimating the difference, in a given sigma_star bin, between the ith and the (i+N/2)th point"; "(N_bin,sigma_star x N_bin,z)/2 Hubble parameter measurements ... combined ... with an inverse-variance weighted average (as also done, e.g. in Moresco et al. 2016; Borghi et al. 2022b)". H(z = 0.8) = 113.1 +- 15.1 (stat) +29.1/-11.3 (syst); "The biggest contribution to this uncertainty is given by the binning scheme".

Schemes without a sigma_star split give the largest systematic difference: "mixing different galaxy populations will exacerbate the progenitor bias (van Dokkum et al. 2000) ... we end up smoothing the evolutionary trend, obtaining a higher H(z) and a larger scatter". "the systematic uncertainty originating from the binning method takes into account the potential progenitor bias". No separate progenitor term.

"to avoid spurious mass-dependent effects, we divided each subsample into two mass bins": SDSS MGS 11 < log M < 11.25 (5210) and 11.25-11.5 (2733); LRGs 11.65-11.9 (1410) and 11.9-12.15 (1049); z > 0.4: 10.6-11 (566) and > 11 (365). "we ensure in each subsample a nearly constant mass as a function of redshift and we avoid mixing the redshift evolution characteristic of different mass regimes".

dz/dD4000n from the difference "between the i-th and the (i + N)-th point for each mass bin"; N = 2 (SDSS MGS), 1 (LRGs), 3 (z > 0.4). The two mass ranges "have been averaged using a weighted mean of the H(z) points at the same redshift, using as weights the corresponding error of each measurement".
Differential approach: "each H(z) point is obtained not by comparing ETGs at z ~ 0 with ETGs at z ~ 1", only neighbouring redshift points within one mass bin are differenced.

Upper envelope: "only the D4000n values above the median D4000n in each redshift bin, and then ... the median"; H from the main analysis and from the upper envelope "compatible within ~ 0.3 sigma on average, and for the majority of the values with differences smaller than 6%". Eq. A.1: H_observed = H_true (1 + Delta_prog bias); "if Delta z_form / Delta z = 0, then there will be no progenitor-bias effect". Table 6 upper limits sigma_prog (own model / van Dokkum & Franx models, km/s/Mpc): z = 0.5929: 6/8; 0.6797: 6/7; 0.7812: 7/9; 0.8754: 10/12; 1.037: 10/13; "on average ~ 0.6 sigma_stat". "we preferred not to add them to the total error budget"; the effect "is expected to be more important for less massive ETGs".

Progenitor bias "is more severe when galaxy samples are compared in wide redshift ranges, but here each H(z) value is estimated within small redshift slices, with Delta z = 0.1"; "the progenitor bias dominates the low-mass range of the distribution, whereas BOSS galaxies have been selected to be the most massive galaxies (log(M/Msun) >~ 11) ... and further divided in bin of velocity dispersion, which is a proxy for stellar mass". No separate progenitor term.

BOSS, 133912 galaxies; "5 velocity dispersion bins: sigma < 150, 150 < sigma < 200, 200 < sigma < 250, 250 < sigma < 300, and sigma > 300 km/s"; stacks in Delta z = 0.025. Difference "between the i-th and the (i + N)-th point for each velocity dispersion subsample. We have chosen N = 4" (Delta z = 0.1). The sigma subsamples are combined in bins of Delta z = 0.025 with "a weighted mean where the weights are the corresponding error of each measurement".

DESI. Median age and mean redshift per bin, error MAD/sqrt(n). "To mitigate progenitor bias (M. Franx 1995; P. G. van Dokkum et al. 2000), we divide the sample into two mass bins according to the median value, log10(M*/Msun) = 11.16"; four equally spaced redshift intervals; "difference between the ith and the (i + N/2)th data points"; values "inverse variance averaged"; H(z = 0.12) = 71.33 +- 3.45 (stat), +- 4.20 total.

H/K = (Ca II H + H-epsilon)/Ca II K; "already a 5% contamination by young populations in the flux budget triggers the inversion"; selects H/K < 1.3 (78 galaxies) plus visual inspection. To "maximise the synchronisation of the sample formation time", an extra cut log(M_formed/Msun) < 10.8 removes 5 galaxies, "removing all the galaxies with z_form < 2"; 39 galaxies; MAD/sqrt(N); H tested with and without two mass bins at the median.

H/K < 1.2. "To evaluate the ageing of galaxies with comparable stellar masses, we divided the sample into two mass bins" at log(M*/Msun) = 11.05; only the pairs HM0-HM1 and LM1-LM2 have enough galaxies and are combined.

Formation-redshift argument: formation redshifts "3.5 < z_f < 5, with a spread in formation age < 0.45 Gyr, which is much smaller than the associated error, therefore avoiding possible progenitor bias issues".
"the use of the small redshift slices Delta z ... controls the effect of some observation biases such as the progenitor bias".

Lists "(iii) the progenitor bias, and (iv) the presence of an underlying young component" among the systematics; (iii) is referred to Moresco+2012 and Moresco+2016; the young component is constrained with the Ca II H/K diagnostic (Sect. 4.1) and a combined selection on UV, emission lines, H-delta and Ca II H/K (Sect. 6).

Progenitor bias "flattens the age - z relations ... producing a biased H(z). The differential approach ... acts to minimize this effect". The upper envelope "by definition, could not be biased by the progenitor bias effect" and agrees with the baseline analysis; conservative estimate "~1% on average, which is negligible"; H in different mass or sigma bins is "mutually consistent, and with no systematic trends".

"Each member of the low-redshift sample has a progenitor which, statistically speaking, is included in the high-redshift sample. But each high-redshift galaxy has some probability of encountering a merger and disappearing from the low-redshift sample"; the age difference is taken from the old edge of the age distribution.
Uses the old edge of the galaxy age distribution: "There is a distinguishable 'red envelope': galaxies are older at lower redshifts."
"These galaxies trace the 'red envelope,' and are the oldest objects in the Universe at every redshift."

Red envelope = edge of the age-redshift relation, found with three algorithms (maximum gradient of the age histogram in redshift bins, Canny edge detection, quantile regression); linear form age/Gyr = a1 (z - z_p) + a0 with z_p = 0.75.

sigma > 280 km/s (363 796 galaxies). "the two slopes for the 280 - 320, and > 320 km s-1 velocity dispersion bins are nearly identical"; "there is a danger of mixing different galaxy mass populations which would directly have a significant (smearing) effect on the derived value of H(z)"; "only the highest velocity dispersion bins (e.g., sigma > 280 km s-1) should be used".
DESI DR1. z_eff (eq. 13) from a weighted linear fit with a common slope across the velocity-dispersion strata.

H/K < 1.2. "Progenitor bias is further limited by our restrictive spectroscopic and velocity dispersion selections (Sects. 3.2 and 3.1) and by the stratification in velocity dispersion. Moreover ... Ditrani et al. (2026) find no evolution in [Fe/H] and [alpha/Fe], indicating that the systems added to the population below z ~ 0.8 were already quenched and chemically mature, so that progenitor bias is negligible in this redshift range".

Relic selection: ultra-compact morphology "minimises the potential risk of mergers and inflow, and thus the risk of combining two progenitor galaxies into composite stellar population"; the 30% of galaxies with the lowest degree of relicness (DoR >~ 0.41) are excluded.
